name: History
notes: Ten courses (40 credits) total; at least six from department faculty; no more than four from outside the department.

The geographical, chronological, and focus-area groups OVERLAP: one course can satisfy multiple distribution requirements at once (e.g. traditional China counts for both Asia and pre-1800), but at least 10 history courses are still required overall. The app counts these groups independently and does not subtract shared courses from the 10-course total.
A grade of C or better is required in the two ULW courses.

Which specific HIST courses fall in each geographic area / chronological period / focus area is maintained on department list pages; the app treats any 200+ HIST course as eligible for these groups (an approximation).

requirementGroups.label: Gateway seminar
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Gateway Seminar (One Course): HIST 200: Introduction to Historical Methods

requirementGroups.label: Geographical distribution (3 areas)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: A minimum of one history course in at least three of the following geographical areas: Africa; Asia and the Pacific; Europe; Latin America; The Middle East; North America.
requirementGroups.note: NEEDS VERIFICATION: per-area course lists are department-maintained; modeled as three distinct HIST courses. Overlaps with chronological/focus groups (allowReuse).

requirementGroups.label: Chronological periods (2 pre-1800 + 2 post-1800)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Four courses, two from each of the following chronological periods: Pre-1800; Post-1800.
requirementGroups.note: NEEDS VERIFICATION: pre/post-1800 designations are department-maintained; modeled as four HIST courses. Overlaps with geographic/focus groups (allowReuse).

requirementGroups.label: Focus area (5 courses in one area)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Five history courses in one of the following focus areas: National or regional; Topical; Methodological.
requirementGroups.note: Focus-area membership is department-maintained (see the concentration PDF). The audit picker records which kind of focus you are pursuing; any HIST course still fills the five-course count. Overlaps with the other distribution groups (allowReuse); the 10-course major total is the binding count.

upperLevelWriting.label: Two W history courses (one at 300-level, one in focus area)
upperLevelWriting.sourceQuote: Two upper-level writing ('W') history courses, one of which must be at the 300-level, and one of which must be in the student's area of focus.
upperLevelWriting.note: The 300-level and focus-area constraints are not auto-enforced.
